chunks: Our Islam is well-known, and our pre-Islamic period (greatness) cannot be denied,
and the Book of Allah gathers for us what was exceptional/distinguished among us,
and it is His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: 'And those of blood relationship are closer [to one another] in the decree of Allah'...
and His Exalted saying: 'Verily, the most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who believe; and Allah is the Guardian of the faithful.'

key_terms.إِسْلَامُنَا: Our Islam (referring to the specific, pure Islam of the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.جَاهِلِيَّتُنَا: Our pre-Islamic period (often implying their virtue even before Islam)

ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha use Quranic verses to establish the superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In this response to Muawiya, Imam Ali (AS) contrasts the enduring, authentic Islam of the Ahl al-Bayt with the lingering 'Jahiliyyah' (pre-Islamic ignorance) of their opponents, asserting that the Quran validates their superior right to kinship and prophetic legacy. By citing Surah Al-Ahzab 33:6 and Surah Ali 'Imran 3:68, he establishes a dual basis for their authority: biological closeness to the Prophet and spiritual adherence to his true followers. This passage underscores the Shia view that the Ahl al-Bayt are the living embodiment of the Quran's teachings, bridging the gap between tribal lineage and divine election.
